full_judgment:
4. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners after placing the petition, and other materials on record mainly argued that the filing of the Execution Case No. 13 of 2003 pending in the 1st Artha Rin Adalat is ex facie barred by both general and special limitation, as provided under Article 182 of the Limitation Act and section 28 of the Ain for which the proceeding including the Order dated 14-6-2005 by which the executing Court admitted the Execution Case is without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 5. In elaborating his argument the learned Counsel further submits that section 28 of Ain provides 180 days for filing an Execution Case and Article 182 of the Limitation Act provides three years. In the present case the final decree was signed on 1-2-2000 and the decree was put in execution i.e. the Execution Case was filed on 13-5-2003 and, as such, under both the laws, general and special, the present money execution case is barred by limitation and on that score execution proceeding is liable to be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The learned Counsel placed reliance on the decision of Nasir Hossain Chaklader vs Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 6 ADC 302 in support of his contention. 

 8. The moot question that faces this Division in this Writ Petition is whether on the admitted fact that the Execution Case was filed on 12-5-2003 after the final decree was passed on 1-2-2000, the limitation under section 28 of the Ain would operate as a bar in admitting the Execution Case. 

 9. As it has been already discussed that admittedly after the passing of the preliminary decree in 1992 final decree was signed on 1-2-2000 and it is also admitted that the Execution Case was filed on 12-5-2003 which is beyond the prescribed limitation for filing the same under section 28 of the Ain and for that reason the executing Court acted illegally in not holding that the Execution case is barred under section 28 (2) of the Ain. Instead of so doing the Executing Court on 14-6-2005 by an Order (Annexure-G) admitted the Execution Case which is certainly beyond its jurisdiction as offended against the express provision of section 28 of the Ain, 2003. 

 Thereafter on 30-10-2002 after 21/2 years of the decree the respondent No. 2, Bank filed Execution Case No. 41 of 2002 against Messrs Shanan Bangladesh Limited only and not against another defendants as Masudul Alam Chaklader who died on 26-7-2002. The execution case was filed with an attested copy of the decree without the certified copy of the original decree. After taking three adjournments on the 4th date on 22-4-2003 the decree-holder bank filed the certified copy of the decree and also the Vokalatnama of the respondent bank and hence the execution case having been filed long after two and half years is hopelessly barred by limitation and, as such, are liable to be rejected as per provisions of section 28 of the Artha Adalat Ain, 2003." 

 13. Fortified with the decision referred to above we are of the view that in all fairness this Rule should succeed. We hold that the Money Execution. Case No. 13 of 2003 pending in the First Artha Rin Adalat, Sherpur is barred by general and special law of limitation as provided under Article 182 of the Limitation Act and section 28 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 respectively. The proceedings of the Money Execution Case No. 13 of 2003 including Order dated 14-6-2005 passed in the said Execution Case are declared to have been proceeded and passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
